subject: Hospitality
title: The Michelin Star System
description: A fast breakdown of The Michelin Star System for builders.

hook.text: Michelin stars—the highest honor in fine dining—were invented by a tire company to sell more rubber.

buildup.text: In 1900, Michelin published a free guide listing gas stations, hotels, and restaurants—to encourage people to drive more.

discovery.text: By 1926, they added star ratings. One star: very good. Two: worth a detour. Three: worth a special journey.

twist.text: Michelin inspectors are anonymous and visit multiple times. Losing a star has driven chefs to depression and even suicide.

climax.text: A three-star rating can double a restaurant's revenue overnight. No other rating system holds this much power over fine dining.

punchline.text: A tire company decides who's the world's best chef. Strange but true.

quiz.question: Why did the Michelin tire company create a restaurant guide?
options: To encourage driving—more driving meant more tire sales
